analysis: Both changed files are documentation only and ship no executable code in this batch. docs/developer/test.md (head lines 177-216) adds the opt-in ModelCheckpointRestoreContentionLiveTests procedure. It uses an isolated ephemeral cache, a scrubbed environment (`env -i`) and an atomically rewritten report. It requires native live and checkpoint precision and does not touch production cache roots or keys. This is consistent with the T-041 guidance on isolated encrypted stores, and it adds no new trust-boundary or secret exposure. docs/reference/ssd-kv-cache.md (head line 119) documents a provider-staged import path that creates destinations from zeroed host bytes and skips eval and stream fences, so staging no longer waits on MLX-Swift's process-wide evalLock. The text says the import plan charges the largest destination as staging scratch. The doc also says the zero source can briefly commit memory outside the MLX allocator, which is a memory-accounting and availability concern (T-041, TB-007, T-029, T-016). The underlying Swift changes (CheckpointHostZeros.swift, CompleteCheckpointTransfer.swift, PagedCheckpointStorage.swift, CompleteCheckpointImportPlan.swift) were not supplied, so the next pass should verify them. It should confirm that: (1) the scratch charge actually covers the largest destination, so a tenant-triggered restore cannot overcommit memory; (2) zero-initialised destinations are fully overwritten, or restore failure paths never expose stale or zero data as a valid prefix (cross-tenant isolation, T-028, T-041); (3) skipping eval and stream fences does not let tensors be read before the copy completes. No findings are reported because the evidence is limited to documentation. The code behaviour is unverified, not shown to be safe.
